chips.title: Enforce the five-finding cap when a review is recorded
chips.summary: Recording a review keeps the five most severe findings as actionable and marks the rest deferred, in a fixed order, and the run records how many review dispatches it used.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.1, the first of Phase 4. It builds on the ported cycle and the Lugos shims, both finished before this board existed, so no prerequisite steps are listed.
Both board files passed the Dias parsers before work began; now writing the failing test for a seven-finding result.
198 tests pass, 16 of them new. A seven-finding review run through the command line recorded five actionable and two deferred, in severity order.
Done. The cap applies to structured findings; a prose reviewer answer is recorded unchanged, so the byte-parity baseline with the Lugos scripts still holds.

chips.title: Keep the recorded findings when a repeat record is refused
chips.summary: A second attempt to record findings for the same review is refused before anything is written, so the first recorded set and its result file stay as they were.

evidence.message: A defect found while landing the finding cap: a refused repeat record replaced the saved findings. Not a plan slice; it protects what the cap writes.
Two new tests failed first, then passed. Through the command line, a refused second record now leaves the seven recorded findings in place; before, it replaced them.
Done. A repeat record is refused before anything is written, and local records take turns, so two at once cannot overwrite each other either.

chips.title: Check an image review against the installed policy before sending
chips.summary: Before a review with screenshots is sent, it is checked against the installed Autowork image policy. A refusal stops with a message; nothing is sent or cut down to text.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.2. It extends the send step that the finding-cap step taught to count dispatches; a refused check must not count as one.
Starting with the failing contract test: a review with a screenshot, checked against the installed Autowork policy.
210 tests pass, 10 of them new for this step. Through the command line, a review with a screenshot was checked as accepted and sent with its image to a stand-in reviewer.
Done. A refused check sends nothing and keeps the claim. The policy tests need Autowork installed, so they ran on this machine and will skip in the hosted test run.

chips.title: Turn a tap on a page into the element it landed on
chips.summary: Given a point on a page, the helper reports the innermost element there as a selector with its data attributes, in a form a finding can carry.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.5. It builds on the browser evidence helpers from the style-guide phase, which finished before this board existed, so no prerequisite steps are listed.
Starting with the failing browser test: a point on the fixture page should come back as the element under it.
221 tests pass, 11 of them new for this step; the browser cases ran here in Chromium. A tap on the fixture's send button came back as that button, and a finding accepted it.
Done. The fixture page has no data attributes and may not be edited, so that half is proven on a small test page, along with nested components and a scrolled tap.

chips.title: Use Impeccable's detector as optional evidence before a review
chips.summary: When the Impeccable tool is installed, its detector runs first and its rule hits go to the review as implementation findings. Without it the run says so and carries on.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.3. The tool is not installed here, so this is built against the real outputs its own repository publishes at the revision the plan inspected.
238 tests pass, 17 of them new for this step. A missing tool or browser is reported and the run carries on; any other failure stops with the tool's own message.
Done, with a limit: it was tested against a stand-in that replays the tool's published output. The real tool is not installed here and has not been run.

chips.title: Tag a release so the new work can be installed
chips.summary: Lugos installs this package from a release tag. A new tag makes the finding cap, the record fix, the image check and the evidence helpers installable.

evidence.message: Not a plan slice: the plan has ux-recast tag a release for Lugos to pin. Moving the Lugos pin is a separate step in the Lugos repository and waits on Matt.
Starting now that the detector step is committed: bump the version, wait for the checks, tag, then prove the tag installs.
The new tag installs into a fresh environment the way Lugos installs it and reports the new version. Automated checks passed on the tagged commit.
Done. Lugos still points at the previous release, so none of this reaches the Lugos entry point until its pin is moved, which waits on Matt.

chips.title: Verify the released package in Lugos before Phase 3 closes
chips.summary: Move Lugos to the tagged package, run its ux-review checks, and record parity evidence so the frozen rubric can safely advance.

evidence.message: Follows the tagged release; confirms the standalone behavior through its Lugos entry point before S4.4 can change the frozen rubric.
Both board files passed Dias validation; inspecting Lugos release and test state before the approved pin change.
origin/master still pins v0.1.0.dev2; changing Lugos needs Matt approval before its ux-review checks can verify parity.
